scenes.title: Bored on the Bank
scenes.summary: Bored on a hot riverbank, Alice's drowsy afternoon breaks when a waistcoated White Rabbit checks his watch and dives down a rabbit-hole, and she impulsively chases after it.

scenes.title: The Long Fall
scenes.summary: Alice falls slowly down a deep well lined with cupboards and bookshelves, musing dreamily about distance, latitude, Antipathies, and her cat Dinah until she thumps down onto sticks and leaves.

scenes.title: The Chase Into the Lamp-Lit Hall
scenes.summary: Unhurt from her fall, Alice sprints down another passage after the hurrying White Rabbit and emerges into a long, low hall lit by lamps.

scenes.title: The Tiny Key and the Garden Door
scenes.summary: Finding every door locked, Alice discovers a tiny golden key on a glass table that opens a fifteen-inch door, revealing a lovely garden she is far too large to enter.

scenes.title: The Drink Me Bottle
scenes.summary: Back at the glass table Alice finds a little bottle labelled DRINK ME that was not there before, and wisely checks first whether it is marked poison.

scenes.title: Shutting Up Like a Telescope
scenes.summary: Finding no poison mark, Alice tastes the nice mixed-flavoured drink and finishes it, shrinking to ten inches tall and delighting that she is now the right size for the garden.

scenes.title: Tears Over the Key
scenes.summary: Unable to reach the little golden key on the table, Alice sits down and cries, then scolds herself sharply for crying and for pretending to be two people.

scenes.title: The EAT ME Cake
scenes.summary: Alice finds a little EAT ME currant cake under the table and hopes it will make her grow or shrink into the garden, eating a bit with no effect before finishing it off.

scenes.title: Growing Tall and Farewell to Feet
scenes.summary: Still growing enormous, Alice comically bids goodbye to her distant feet and plans to send them Christmas boots by carrier.

scenes.title: Locked Out and the Pool of Tears
scenes.summary: Now nine feet high, Alice hits the roof, cannot fit through the garden door, scolds herself and weeps gallons of tears that form a deep pool.

scenes.title: The Rabbit's Return and Fright
scenes.summary: The White Rabbit returns hurrying in fine dress with gloves and fan, muttering about the Duchess; when Alice timidly speaks to him, he starts violently, drops his fan and gloves, and flees into the darkness.

scenes.title: Fanning and Who in the World Am I
scenes.summary: Alice picks up the fan and gloves and fans herself, puzzling over whether she was changed in the night; doubting she is Ada or Mabel, she fails her multiplication and geography and resolves to test herself with lessons.

scenes.title: The Wrong Words and Lonely Tears
scenes.summary: Alice recites the little crocodile with wrong, hoarse words, concludes tearfully she must be Mabel, vows to stay down here, then breaks down wishing they would come for her, tired of being all alone.

scenes.title: Shrinking Narrow Escape and Splash
scenes.summary: Alice realizes the fan is shrinking her, narrowly stops at two feet high, finds the garden still shut, then slips splash into her own salt pool of tears.

scenes.title: The Mouse in the Pool
scenes.summary: Alice spots a mouse swimming in the pool and tries addressing it in English, then in French with 'Ou est ma chatte?', which frightens it and provokes an angry outburst about cats.

scenes.title: The Promise and the Crowded Shore
scenes.summary: Alice soothes the mouse but offends it again by praising her cat Dinah and a farm dog, then coaxes it back by promising silence on cats and dogs; the mouse agrees to tell its history on shore as Alice leads the now crowded party of fallen birds and animals out of the pool.

scenes.title: Wet Crowd on the Bank
scenes.summary: The soaked birds and animals gather shivering on the bank. Alice argues with the Lory about age while the authoritative Mouse calls them to sit in a ring to get dry.

scenes.title: The Driest Thing I Know
scenes.summary: The Mouse pompously recites dry William the Conqueror history to dry them. Interruptions from the Lory and Duck annoy it, and Alice admits she is still wet as ever.

scenes.title: Caucus-Race and Prizes
scenes.summary: The Dodo proposes a chaotic Caucus-race with no rules. Everyone runs, dries off, everybody wins, and Alice awards comfits and solemnly receives a thimble prize.

scenes.title: A Long and Sad Tale
scenes.summary: Alice asks for the Mouse's long sad tale. She pictures it as a tail-shape about Fury and the mouse while missing the point, offending the Mouse until it stalks away despite pleas.

scenes.title: Dinah Scatters Them All
scenes.summary: Alice innocently praises her cat Dinah for catching mice and birds, panicking the whole party into fleeing. Left alone, she regrets mentioning Dinah and cries lonely until footsteps approach.

scenes.title: Mistaken for Mary Ann
scenes.summary: The anxious White Rabbit returns searching for his fan and gloves and mistakes Alice for his housemaid Mary Ann, ordering her home. Frightened, Alice runs to the little house marked W. RABBIT to fetch them.

scenes.title: The Rabbit's Errand
scenes.summary: Inside the Rabbit's tidy room, Alice muses about going messages for a rabbit and imagines Dinah ordering her about, then finds the fan and gloves and impulsively drinks from a little unlabelled bottle, hoping it will make her grow large again.

scenes.title: The Uncomfortable Growth
scenes.summary: The bottle works far too fast, and Alice grows explosively until she is wedged with head against the ceiling, one arm out of the window and one foot up the chimney, trapped and miserable in the little room.

scenes.title: Lonely Reflection
scenes.summary: Stuck and unable to leave, Alice grows lonely and reflective, missing home, wondering about being stuck in a fairy-tale, aging, and lessons, until a voice outside interrupts her self-conversation.

scenes.title: The Arm in the Window
scenes.summary: The Rabbit demands his gloves and finds the door blocked by Alice's giant elbow. He tries the window, gets grabbed at, falls into a cucumber-frame, and with Pat stares at the huge arm filling the window, too afraid to pull it away.

scenes.title: Bill Goes Down the Chimney
scenes.summary: Reinforcements arrive with ladders and ropes and send Bill down the chimney. Alice kicks him sky-high like a rocket. After brandy and confusion, the Rabbit threatens to burn the house down and Alice threatens back with Dinah.

scenes.title: Pebble Cakes and Escape
scenes.summary: The besiegers shower pebbles through the window that magically turn to cakes. Alice eats one, shrinks small enough to escape, dashes past the crowd nursing Bill, and flees safely into the thick wood.

scenes.title: Play with the Giant Puppy
scenes.summary: Resolving to regain her size and find the garden, Alice meets an enormous puppy. She coaxes it, plays fetch with a stick behind a thistle while fearing being trampled, then escapes when it tires and pants.

scenes.title: The Caterpillar Revealed
scenes.summary: Resting and wondering how to grow again, Alice finds a large mushroom and peeps over its top to come face to face with a large blue caterpillar smoking a hookah in silence.

scenes.title: Who Are You?
scenes.summary: Alice meets the silent, hookah-smoking Caterpillar on the mushroom. Its languid but stern questioning about who she is irritates and confuses her, ending with its curt advice to keep her temper.

scenes.title: A Wrong Recitation
scenes.summary: Alice admits she has changed and cannot remember things. At the Caterpillar's order she melancholily recites 'You are old, Father William,' with all the words altered, which the Caterpillar declares wrong from beginning to end.

scenes.title: The Mushroom Clue
scenes.summary: Arguing over size, Alice offends the three-inch-high Caterpillar by calling three inches wretched. It calms, then crawls away, leaving the cryptic clue that one side of the mushroom makes her taller and the other shorter.

scenes.title: Shrinking Violently
scenes.summary: Alone with the round mushroom, Alice breaks off both sides and experiments. Nibbling the right-hand bit violently shrinks her until her chin strikes her foot, forcing her to frantically eat the other bit.

scenes.title: Serpent in the Trees
scenes.summary: Freed with an immense serpent-like neck towering over the trees, Alice is attacked by a frantic Pigeon guarding its eggs. Despite her protests that she is a little girl, the Pigeon insists she is a serpent looking for eggs.

scenes.title: Back to the Right Size
scenes.summary: Alice denies wanting raw eggs and is dismissed by the sulky Pigeon. Carefully nibbling both mushroom pieces, she returns to her usual height and then shrinks to nine inches to approach a little house by the beautiful garden.

scenes.title: The Footmen's Invitation
scenes.summary: Alice watches from the wood as a fish-faced footman delivers the Queen's croquet invitation to a frog-faced footman; their solemn bows tangle their curls and Alice laughs and retreats.

scenes.title: Nonsense at the Door
scenes.summary: Alice tries to knock and enter but the frog footman sitting by the door argues in nonsense circles while howling, sneezing, and crashing continue inside, capped by a plate flying at his head; exasperated, Alice opens the door herself.

scenes.title: Pepper-Filled Kitchen
scenes.summary: Alice steps into a smoke-filled, pepper-choked kitchen where the Duchess nurses a howling baby, the cook stirs soup, and only the cook and a grinning Cheshire Cat do not sneeze; Alice politely asks about the grin.

scenes.title: Saucepans and Lullaby
scenes.summary: Conversation curdles as the cook hurls fire-irons and dishes at the Duchess and baby, the Duchess growls about minding business and calls to chop off Alice's head, then violently rocks the baby while singing a rough lullaby with cook and baby howling the chorus.

scenes.title: The Baby Turns Into a Pig
scenes.summary: The Duchess flings the baby to Alice and rushes off to croquet; Alice carries the strange starfish-like creature outside to save it, watches its face turn to a snout and its grunts deepen, then sets it down relieved as it trots into the wood a handsome pig.

scenes.title: We're All Mad Here
scenes.summary: In the wood Alice respectfully questions the grinning, clawed Cheshire Cat on a bough about which way to go; the Cat playfully declares Hatter and March Hare both mad, proves its own madness by purring and tail-wagging, mentions croquet, vanishes and reappears to hear the baby became a pig.

scenes.title: Grin Without a Cat
scenes.summary: Alice walks toward the March Hare, the Cat reappears to quibble pig or fig then vanishes slowly tail-first leaving its grin lingering; marveling at a grin without a cat, Alice timidly approaches the ear-chimneyed, fur-thatched house after nibbling mushroom to grow.

scenes.title: No Room at the Tea Table
scenes.summary: Alice discovers the tea table under the tree and sits down uninvited, trading rude first remarks about wine, manners, and her hair with the March Hare and Hatter while the Dormouse sleeps between them.

scenes.title: The Raven Riddle
scenes.summary: The Hatter poses the unanswerable riddle of the raven and writing-desk, leading to pedantic wordplay about saying what you mean and a sleepy interjection from the Dormouse before an awkward silence.

scenes.title: The Funny Watch
scenes.summary: The Hatter obsesses over his broken watch that shows the day but not the hour, blaming butter in the works, leaving Alice puzzled while he pours tea on the sleeping Dormouse.

scenes.title: Wasting Time
scenes.summary: Alice gives up the riddle and is lectured that Time is a person who will not stand being beaten, with fanciful talk of twisting the clock from lessons to dinner-time.

scenes.title: Always Tea-Time
scenes.summary: The Hatter tells how he quarreled with Time after murdering his Twinkle song for the Queen of Hearts, condemning them to endless six o'clock and perpetual moving round the tea-things.

scenes.title: The Treacle-Well Sisters
scenes.summary: Pressed to tell a story, the Dormouse begins the tale of Elsie, Lacie and Tillie living on treacle at the bottom of a well, constantly derailed by Alice's questions and quarrels over taking more tea.

scenes.title: Drawings of Muchness
scenes.summary: The Dormouse insists it was a treacle-well and the sisters drew treacle and M-things; the party shifts places with spilled milk, and Alice grows bewildered as the Dormouse drifts into sleep.

scenes.title: Leaving the Tea-Party
scenes.summary: Insulted by the Hatter, Alice storms off while they try to put the Dormouse in the teapot, finds a door in a tree, and returns through the long hall to finally enter the beautiful garden.

scenes.title: Painting the Roses Red
scenes.summary: Alice discovers three card-gardeners frantically painting white roses red and learns they fear beheading by the Queen, just as the Queen's approach is announced.

scenes.title: The Grand Arrival
scenes.summary: The grand royal procession files in: soldiers, courtiers, royal children, guests including the White Rabbit, the Knave bearing the crown, and finally the King and Queen of Hearts.

scenes.title: Alice Stands Her Ground
scenes.summary: Alice refuses to lie down, boldly defies the Queen's cry of Off with her head, hides the three gardeners in a flower-pot to save them, and is drafted to join the Queen for croquet.

scenes.title: A Whispered Warning
scenes.summary: Walking with the procession, Alice shares a nervous whispered aside with the White Rabbit, who reveals the Duchess is under sentence of execution.

scenes.title: Chaotic Croquet Ground
scenes.summary: The absurd croquet game begins with live flamingos, hedgehogs, and soldiers as arches; the Queen's constant cries of execution leave Alice uneasy and looking for escape.

scenes.title: The Grin Returns
scenes.summary: The Cheshire Cat's grin appears, giving Alice a welcome friend to confide in about the unfair game, until she cleverly flatters the listening Queen.

scenes.title: A Cat May Look at a King
scenes.summary: The King dislikes the Cat and demands its removal; the Queen orders its beheading and the King rushes off to fetch the executioner.

scenes.title: Lost Mallet and Ball
scenes.summary: Alice wanders back to the confused game to retrieve her hedgehog and runaway flamingo, finding turns and arches have vanished.

scenes.title: To Behead a Grin
scenes.summary: A crowd debates how to behead a head without a body; Alice defers to the Duchess, who is summoned just as the Cat fades away entirely.

scenes.title: The Pleasant Temper and the Pepper Rule
scenes.summary: The Duchess tucks her arm affectionately into Alice's as they walk off together. Alice is glad to find her in such a pleasant temper and decides it must have been the pepper that made her savage in the kitchen, musing on a new rule that pepper makes people hot-tempered and sweet things make children sweet-tempered.

scenes.title: Everything's Got a Moral
scenes.summary: The Duchess squeezes close to Alice, resting her uncomfortably sharp chin on Alice's shoulder, and insists everything's got a moral. She moralizes love, minding one's business, flamingoes and mustard biting, and a mustard-mine, while Alice grows uncomfortable but politely corrects her.

scenes.title: The Right to Think and Pigs Flying
scenes.summary: Alice cannot follow the Duchess's tangled moral about being what you seem, asks her not to continue, and privately scorns the cheap present of sayings. Prodded again by the sharp chin, Alice answers sharply that she has a right to think, prompting the Duchess's retort about pigs flying.

scenes.title: The Queen Interrupts
scenes.summary: The mood snaps to fear as the frowning Queen appears, threatens the Duchess with beheading, and the Duchess vanishes instantly, leaving frightened Alice to follow the Queen back to the game.

scenes.title: Executions and a Pardon
scenes.summary: Croquet resumes under terror as the Queen shouts for executions, arrests leave no arches, then she asks Alice about the Mock Turtle while the King quietly pardons everyone.

scenes.title: The Lazy Gryphon Wakes
scenes.summary: Alice is handed to the sleeping Gryphon by the departing Queen; the Gryphon wakes, chuckles, and reveals the comforting secret that the Queen never really executes anybody.

scenes.title: Meeting the Sorrowful Mock Turtle
scenes.summary: Led to a lonely, sighing Mock Turtle on the rocks, Alice pities his great sorrow, sits down at his command, and hears his mournful opening: once, I was a real Turtle.

scenes.title: Tortoise the Master
scenes.summary: The Mock Turtle calms enough to tell of school in the sea under an old Turtle master called Tortoise, scolds Alice as very dull for questioning the name, and the Gryphon shames her before urging him to drive on.

scenes.title: Extras and the Regular Course
scenes.summary: The Mock Turtle describes daily sea-school education, prized extras of French, music, and washing, and the regular course of Reeling and Writhing with Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision, while Alice is silenced for not knowing uglifying.

scenes.title: Mystery Lessons That Lessen
scenes.summary: The comic lesson-list continues with Mystery, Seaography, Drawling, Stretching, Laughing and Grief, and ten-hour days that lessen daily, until the Gryphon cuts lessons short to turn to games.

scenes.title: How the Lobster Quadrille Is Danced
scenes.summary: The Mock Turtle recovers from sobs to describe the Lobster Quadrille, with the Gryphon interrupting excitedly. Together they build the dance step by step - forming lines, clearing jelly-fish, advancing with lobsters, throwing them out to sea, somersaulting and returning - growing wilder until they suddenly fall quiet.

scenes.title: The Dance and the Whiting's Song
scenes.summary: Alice agrees to see the dance. The Mock Turtle and Gryphon solemnly dance round her, treading on her toes, while the Mock Turtle slowly and sadly sings the whiting and snail invitation to join the dance.

scenes.title: Why the Whiting Has Its Tail in Its Mouth
scenes.summary: Curious about the song, Alice asks about whitings. The Mock Turtle and Gryphon explain with solemn nonsense why whitings have their tails in their mouths, why they are called whiting, and what soles and eels have to do with boots and shoes.

scenes.title: With What Porpoise?
scenes.summary: Talk turns from the porpoise in the song to a pun on porpoise and purpose. The Mock Turtle takes offense at correction, and the Gryphon impatiently demands to hear Alice's adventures instead of explanations.

scenes.title: Alice Tells Her Adventures
scenes.summary: Alice nervously recounts her adventures since the White Rabbit while the two creatures listen wide-eyed and quiet. Intrigued that her recitation to the Caterpillar came out wrong, they order her to stand up and repeat a lesson.

scenes.title: The Garbled Lessons
scenes.summary: Feeling back at school, Alice recites a garbled Lobster version of the sluggard poem and then the Owl and Panther pie verse. The Mock Turtle and Gryphon find it curious nonsense and demand explanations, then tell her to leave off.

scenes.title: Turtle Soup Interrupted
scenes.summary: Offered another dance figure or a song, Alice chooses a song. The Mock Turtle sobs through 'Beautiful Soup' until a distant cry of the trial beginning interrupts. The Gryphon seizes Alice's hand and hurries her away as the soup refrain fades behind them.

scenes.title: The Court Assembled
scenes.summary: Alice arrives at the crowded courtroom with the King and Queen on the throne, the chained Knave, and the dish of tarts. She observes the judge, jury-box, and jurors busily writing, steals Bill the Lizard's squeaking pencil, and takes in the absurd pomp.

scenes.title: The Accusation Read
scenes.summary: Trumpets sound as the White Rabbit formally reads the accusation verse about the stolen tarts. The King rushes to verdict before being corrected, setting the pompous, nonsensical legal tone.

scenes.title: First Witness: The Hatter
scenes.summary: The Hatter enters still holding tea and bread-and-butter. Questioned about dates and his hat, he grows pale under the Queen's stare while the King threatens execution if he is nervous.

scenes.title: Growing Pains
scenes.summary: Alice feels herself beginning to grow larger again, squeezing the Dormouse beside her. They bicker about growing, and the offended Dormouse sulkily crosses to the other side of the court.

scenes.title: Twinkling Tea Evidence
scenes.summary: Under pressure the trembling Hatter stammers about thin bread-and-butter and twinkling tea. The King puns on T, the March Hare hastily denies speaking, and the Dormouse sleeps through his cue.

scenes.title: Poor Speaker Dismissed
scenes.summary: The Hatter cannot recall what the Dormouse said and pleads poverty. Cheering guinea-pigs are suppressed in a canvas bag, the Hatter is stood down and dismissed, and the Queen orders his head taken off as he flees shoeless.

scenes.title: Pepper, Confusion, and Alice!
scenes.summary: The pepper-carrying cook refuses to give evidence, answers only that tarts are made of pepper, and sparks royal fury at the sleepy Dormouse. In the confusion the cook vanishes, and to Alice's shock she herself is called as the next witness.

scenes.title: The Jury-Box Upset
scenes.summary: Alice jumps up and overturns the jury-box, scattering the jurymen like goldfish. She apologetically gathers them up and rights the upside-down Lizard while the King gravely demands order.

scenes.title: Important or Unimportant
scenes.summary: The King questions Alice, who knows 'nothing whatever.' He declares it very important, is corrected to unimportant, and the jury confusedly writes down both versions.

scenes.title: Rule Forty-Two
scenes.summary: The King invents Rule Forty-two to expel anyone over a mile high. Alice refuses to leave, mocks the rule, and the King pales and hastily calls for a verdict.

scenes.title: The Mysterious Verses
scenes.summary: The White Rabbit produces a newly found paper. Undirected, unsigned, and not in the Knave's hand, it turns out to be verses. The King orders it read from beginning to end.

scenes.title: Explaining the Unexplainable
scenes.summary: The nonsense verses are read. Alice offers sixpence to anyone who can explain them. The King triumphantly finds proof in swimming, tarts, and fits, ending with an unlaughed-at pun.

scenes.title: Sentence First - Rebellion
scenes.summary: The Queen demands sentence before verdict. Alice rebels, defies the Queen, and declares them only cards. The whole pack flies at her, and her dream shatters into waking.

scenes.title: Waking on the Bank
scenes.summary: Alice finds herself on the bank with her head in her sister's lap. She recounts her curious dream, then runs off to tea, marveling at Wonderland.

scenes.title: Her Sister's Daydream
scenes.summary: Left alone at sunset, her sister half-dreams Wonderland alive around her, then imagines reality beneath it and future grown Alice keeping her child-heart to tell the tale to other children.
